blocks.text: Nehemiah 11’s account of resettling Jerusalem belongs to a larger sequence in which the city is repopulated, its wall is dedicated with two thanksgiving processions, and provisions are arranged for offerings that support priests and Levites. The book also combines vivid first-person memoir material with third-person narrative, lists, material concerning Ezra, and editorial transitions; how these parts relate is disputed, so the chapter is best read as part of that varied larger presentation rather than as a simple uninterrupted autobiography.

sections.title: The larger movement of the story
